detail:
Sources list the identification and avoidance of personal triggers as a core management pillar. The ASCIA 2025 position paper lists "identification and avoidance of triggers (e.g. allergens, physical)" among its core management recommendations. A GI primer by Weinstock et al. (2020) lists trigger avoidance as first-line, naming stress, heat, and alcohol. The MSD Manuals (Professional) names physical touch, exercise, alcohol, NSAIDs, opioids, insect stings, and foods as reported triggers.

An important nuance comes from a patient-perspective paper summarized by AJMC: it cautions that aggressive avoidance can drive social isolation. Triggers also vary from person to person, so the relevant trigger list is an individual one.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor — ideally one familiar with mast cell disorders — about identifying and managing your own triggers.
sourceName: ASCIA (Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy)

Weinstock et al.'s 2020 primer lists trigger avoidance as first-line, naming stress, heat, and alcohol.
The MSD Manuals names physical touch, exercise, alcohol, NSAIDs, opioids, insect stings, and foods as reported triggers.
Nuance: a patient-perspective paper cautions that aggressive avoidance can drive social isolation. Triggers vary person to person. Talk to your doctor about your own trigger picture.
title: Identifying and avoiding personal triggers
